title: [科幻] 太空版人生游戏：光年卡农
summary:
https://iron-bamboo.interimm.org/
我和朋友们一直在做一个叫做星际移民中心的硬科幻项目，从 2012 年左右一直到现在。最近有豆瓣友邻反应说太枯燥了，说不如出个游戏。于是就跟 Claude 一起开发了这个游戏。
游戏的核心是人生游戏 + 未来五百年左右的时间设定。一段话说一下基础的背景设定：起初就是太阳系内部的一些开发，后来出现一个可以跟脉冲星产生拍频的信号，有了通信，但是双方都无法飞到对方那么远。再后来出现了 Kraniskov tube,可以有可小物件的交换，再后来就是可以载人。然后通道的扩展，大家都可以去其他地方生活。其中铁竹号是一艘 Krasnikov tube 维护飞船。
游戏就是这样背景下，随机出生，经历历史上的一些事件，自己做出选择，然后死去，然后后代或者朋友或者其它人继续沿着你的路线探索生活，再死去。
因为每个人的人生交叉延后，就像卡农一样，所以起名字叫做光年卡农。
===
因为我和朋友们是理工科加艺术背景，比如我是理论物理 PhD 学位，毕业后做一些 AI 的应用和研发，所以整个项目的基本就是科学上要有方程可解的那种硬科幻。这个游戏我们也想尽量引入一些硬核的设定，但是由于太过遥远，有些只好做出假设，可能物理上会有一点解释不通，但是为了能够继续推进故事，我们不得已只能这样简化了。

summary:

项目
数字




全球服务器收入

x86 服务器
919 亿，+16%

744 亿，+146%

非 x86 涨这么猛，基本就是 GPU 整机和 Arm 那一套。
但 x86 这边芯片其实也没闲着：至强 6+ 最多 288 个能效核，AMD 新一代 EPYC 最多 256 核，双路一台就 500 多核了。
我们是做服务器维保的，自己的感觉：
新预算大部分去了 GPU ，通用服务器的采购往后拖
在用的老 x86 机器服役时间就会越拉越长，内存、硬盘、电源这些迟早要换
AI 智能体要调工具、跑程序，最后还是落在普通 CPU 机器上，所以 x86 不会真被冷落
想问下大家公司里现在什么情况：通用服务器还在正常换代，还是能撑就撑？

title: [分享创造] Jev 做 arXiv 大规模文献检索综述， 5 分钟筛 36,000 篇论文
summary:
设计动机
人工智能领域的论文进入爆发式增长，数量越来越多，文献检索也面临着很大的挑战。我个人在使用 General/Coding Agent 进行文献检索（寻找相关工作或者领域梳理）的时能体验到的局限性：
通用 agent 通过黑盒 web search api 进行开放网络检索，通常只能拿到 top-k ，难以穷举并且难以回答“这里领域有多少篇论文”的问题；
通用 agent 通过 search api 进行的检索噪音大，返回的内容是整个互联网的相关性条目，需要花费额外的开销进行数据清洗和整理；
上述局限性导致 agent 在查找文献的时候浅尝辄止，或者开销大/速度慢。所以在上半年的时候我给自己 vibe coding 了一套 arXiv 元数据抓取->向量化->关键词或语义召回->LLM 精筛的管线。但成本仍然比较高，并且精筛时候速度很慢，用起来不怎么顺手。
九月中旬的时候 Jev 横空出世，我意识到非常适合用来做召回后的文献精筛和分类，于是就开始重构自己的文献基础设施，把它迁移到 Jev 上来。可以先通过一张 GIF 示意图感受精筛的速度：

我把这个系统命名为 Parallax ，其实它不止是一个文献检索工具，还包括了一系列的论文阅读、综述产出工作流。项目已投入生产环境，欢迎注册试用： https://parallax.ink
下面将继续介绍系统搭建时的一些设计和感悟。
检索结构
曾过一段时间的推荐算法但没太接触过 Agentic Search 领域，还带着点相关的思维定势，所以最初的设想是通过一个漏斗式的结构完成召回、粗筛、精筛。后来发现论文检索的特点跟信息流推荐还很不一样：
需要扩增：论文存在引用关系，通过一篇早期文章的引用关系进行扩增检索是很常见的手段
需要补充：不管是人还是 Agent 进行检索的过程都会有疏漏的可能，所以在初次检索完成后还要进行复核，看看是否有不合适的条目被纳入，或者是否有早些关注到的标记点被遗漏
这样的话漏斗式的检索显然就不够用了，结合多路召回所需的合并去重、假阳性需要批量剔除，我发现集合运算是解决这个问题的良好数据结构，因此就将整套检索的底层架构用集合代数的接口重写了一遍。
因此检索结构设计为：Agentic 操作的基本单元是论文集合（满足确定性、互异性、无序性的基本属性），支持并集、差集等基本的集合运算符；同时引入了一些实用的功能性对象或算子：
虚拟根：用一个虚拟对象表示检索起点，比如全库论文集合、arXiv 每日公告的论文集合；使用虚拟根是为了避免对大规模条目进行持久化，占用过多存储空间
规则过滤：通过 arXiv 分类标签、时间窗口、资源种类、embedding 相似度、关键词检索等条件进行论文条目过滤
AI 精筛：利用 Jev/LLM 进行条件判定，条件是由 agent 根据用户意图生成的
AI 分类：利用 Jev 的多标签概率判定接口进行分类，不过一篇论文可以同时归属两个分类，所以这块的分类没有设计互斥性
我把整个检索系统用节点图的形式进行可视化，前端使用 ReactFlow 构建。节点图的形式足够灵活，能够应对各种不同的生产需求。

于是一个典型的节点工作流如上图所示：使用关键词或者语义检索进行多路召回，然后用并集算子进行合并去重得到一个规模较大的候选集，扔到 AI 精筛节点调用 Jev 进行精筛（目前判定阈值硬编码为 0.5 ），再通过 AI 分类节点进行主题分类。
在 DeepSeek-Flash 模型实测中大部分时候 Agent 会依照典型的工作流进行检索，但面临更大规模更复杂的检索需求，Agent 可能会在复核过程中发现工作疏漏，构建用于弥补的新集合，反复调试出“最终版”集合，再进入下一步分类阶段，从而构建出跟电路图一样复杂的工作流：

相比于 General/Coding Agent 的文本文件记账直接处理、结构化标记语言（ XML/JSON ）记账脚本处理，建立在数据库和索引基础上的集合记账能够实现更大规模、更高效的处理；并且将这种大规模处理任务委托给确定性的程序，能够对抗模型的幻觉或者上下文压缩过程中的记忆细节丢失。集合数据结构还可以进一步扩展统计分析接口，以满足更加精细的数据洞察需求。
性能和成本
其实上述的思路非常自然，ComfyUI 等低代码节点图工作流已经深入人心，在很多人的脑海中应该都浮现过类似的文献检索思路。但是让这样的系统能够投入生产使用，最大的问题不是数据抽象，而是面临较大规模数据时的性能优化，以及如何平衡速度、成本、效果这几个维度。
Parallax 目前通过 OAI 接口抓取了 arXiv 下 cs.*分类自 2020 年来的元数据更新，大概有 82 万篇，元数据及其索引约占 7.8GB ；为了实现语义召回，系统接入 Perplerxity 的完成语义嵌入，向量比元数据重得多。每篇论文的摘要经 pplx-embed-v1-0.6b 嵌入成 1024 维向量。按 float32 算单条 4KB ，82 万篇理论上约 3.3GB ；如果压成 halfvec 半精度表示，单条 2KB 共计约 1.65GB 。但这只是裸数据大小。真正落到 PostgreSQL+pgvector 里，为了同时满足精确和快速两个目标，向量实际存了多份，加上索引的总占用达到了约 17GB 。
关于系统的一些优化手段：
精确语义检索的召回分批：直接跑一条大规模召回 SQL 时长不可控，并且发生中断缺乏检查点又要重新跑，因此对召回语句按时间窗口进行分批检索 top-K ，最后合并再取总 top-K ，精确性得以确保；分批会带来一定的额外时间开销，但是系统可靠性和资源可控性都获得了提升。
近似最近邻（ ANN ）：系统实测发现在 top-K 召回任务下，随着 K 的增加，召回率相比于精确算法会下降，这是由于 HNSW 索引本身的特点导致的；因此我们采用的策略是在较小的 K 时采用 ANN 进行加速，能从精确版本所需的十多秒降至几秒，并且召回准确率能保持在 90%以上。
Jev 的批处理和并发：我们的精筛和分类都使用 Jev 的 noul 元语实现，分类也使用 noul 是面向论文主题的多标签场景；在实现上，对同一个节点任务在后台切分批次，并发推进，精筛和分类的批大小并不是固定的，而是根据 Jev 的上下文窗口和当前批内元数据 token 长度自适应调整。
相比于最初使用的 DeepSeek-Flash 进行精筛，九月下旬切换到 Jev 后在生产服务器上实测，新管线对 36,564 篇论文进行精筛判定只花了 5 分钟左右，是 LLM 版本速度的 10+倍，而成本只有不到五分之一。
为什么 LLM 的成本会高延迟会低？因为我们设计的管线会收集判定审计信息（概率或者原因），LLM 并非直接输出 true 或者 false ，而是输出一个带判定结果和原因的 JSON 。如果打开模型的 CoT 思考，模型的思考长度不可控故而延迟不可控；如果关闭模型的 CoT 思考，又会导致批处理时时常出现 JSON 格式错误，要么整批作废重试、要么聚集错误结果开新批次。不管怎么样，在专门为 type-safe 设计的 Jev 面前，LLM 都并非解决这个问题的首选。
实测效果
在一个“LLM 智能体记忆机制”主题的论文检索案例中，Agent 会先根据用户提供的线索对库中的论文进行低成本探针（ probe ）调研搞清楚论文的大致分布情况，然后创建 6 路关键词+5 路语义召回，合并后得到三万多篇候选文献； Agent 会拟定提供给 Jev 进行判定的业务标准，什么样的论文可以被纳入（ include ），什么样的论文需要被剔除（ exclude ），然后提交后台进行并发批处理判定。

而在另一个“多模态理解与统一多模态方向八月份工作梳理”主题的检索任务中，Agent 通过三路关键词和语义召回得到 466 篇候选文献后进入精筛管线得到 428 篇匹配主题的论文，接着 Agent 读取集合条目标题拟定分类目录后，调用 Jev 分类节点进行分类，得到评测基准与数据集、具身智能、安全隐私、理解生成统一等 10 类。
用户指出评测基准这类还有一百多篇，可以进一步细分，Agent 就继续探查条目，对评测子集进行进一步细分，得到 11 个类别的评测基准与数据子类别。分类过程中 Jev 会提供论文条目关于每一类分类判定标准的纳入概率，这些概率信息都会被持久化到数据库中以供用户和 Agent 审查。

集成工作流
为了让检索的结果能够更便捷地转化为用户对于论文的理解和对领域的洞察，我在数据与检索基础设施之上，构建了整套云原生的 Agentic Workflow 。产品追求智能体原生，所以为所有功能都设计了供 Agent 调用的工具入口；而人类目前仍然需要在学术研究场景进行深度介入，所以我们仍重视用户的交互习惯与系统的可观测性，为大部分功能都构建了可视化的 UI 面板（比如更适合文献阅读场景的衬线+两端对齐阅读排版）。

用户可以利用 Parallax 提供的技能，直接产出领域研究综述、每日/每周/每月进展跟踪报告：

Why Parallax?
Why Parallax?
为什么要设计 Parallax ？在 RSI 真正到来、AI 领域论文的价值完全消散之前，对于 Frontier Lab 以外的学者、学生或开发者来说，arXiv 上的论文仍然是第一手的领域信息来源；但现在论文的产出量越来越大、文献所涵盖的总体洞察越来越多，但是人们却越来越难以获得与论文增长相匹配的、对领域洞察和理解的增长。
我希望能找全文献，看看整个领域或者某个我所关注的细分方向，在空间或者时间维度上发生了什么，要做到这一点就只能对全量论文做快速的召回扫描，而无法仅仅通过 Google Search 或者 arXiv Search 的 top-K 结果来实现这一点。“找全文献”这件事情的需求，从 GitHub 上琳琅满目的 awesome paper list 就可见一斑；而设计 Parallax 就是为了能快速自助产出 awesome paper list ，并且通过更易用的数据接口和更聚焦的上下文管理来在此基础上更全面地理解领域发生或者正在发生的事情。
我一年半之前还在游戏行业工作的时候曾看过用户研究部门的分享，介绍他们是如何助力游戏战投部门的工作的。游戏玩得多的人都知道，游戏的品类是很难定义的，因为玩法之间的分类往往是模糊的，而一款游戏可以有很多种玩法，品类定义起来也更加麻烦。但是定义品类、预测品类的走向又是用户研究和战略投资绕不开的课题，因为每隔一段时间就会有一种新品类在市面上流行起来，对于大厂来说对未来可能的新品类进行提前布局是必要的商业手段。那如何解决这个问题呢？
Steam 以及一些游戏直播平台上有大量的游戏评价数据，并且 Steam 游戏的标签系统是用户共建的。通过建设评价数据和标签的实时观测系统，能够看到一种标签或者评论区中的概括是如何从零碎的短语，演变成为大部分玩家的共同描述手段，从而成为一种新的“品类”。比如“魂-like”或者“类银河战士恶魔城游戏”就是从用户标签或者评价中起源，并逐步演变为约定俗成的正式品类名称；而最初用户想表达的意思仅仅只是“该款游戏的玩法像银河战士和恶魔城”或者“游戏的操作难度和叙事像黑魂”。
而 arXiv 文献数量的暴涨，也让 AI 学术研究进入了高频、高动态的时期；而 Jev 的到来让我发现能够通过一种更加低成本的方式来灵活地观察领域的变化和动向。
Parallax 现在已经上线生产环境，欢迎来访使用： https://parallax.ink

title: [推广] Grok、Cursor、X 联合会员怎么开？ ChongGrok 已支持代订阅
summary:
我负责 ChongGrok 的运营。我们已经上线了 Grok 、Cursor 、X 联合会员代订阅服务，支持支付宝、微信付款，以及提供开票服务。最近在关注这套新会员的朋友，可以先看下面的档位和开通说明，再决定是否需要办理。
这次合并的官方名称是 The X Subscription。10 月 12 日的官方公告把 Grok 、Cursor 和 X 的会员权益纳入同一套订阅，Premium 及以上还包含 Grok Bot 的使用。如果你同时用 Grok 查资料、用 Cursor 写代码、在 X 上发内容，现在可以通过一份联合订阅获得相应权益，具体功能和用量取决于所选档位。
选档位前，先弄清两件事：Grok 和 Cursor 共用每周用量； Cursor 里的 Claude 、GPT 等第三方模型另行按量计费。新套餐的共享用量按所选档位计算，不能把几份旧套餐的额度直接相加。
四个档位，先看功能，再看用量
目前个人付费方案有四档。以下按官方美元月价和Cursor 套餐功能整理，价格不含可能在结账时加收的税费：
Plus：8 美元/月。 基础用量，可以使用 Grok 和 Cursor 自有模型，关联个人 X 账号后获得 X Premium 权益；不含 Grok Bot 、Cursor 云端代理和第三方模型。
Premium：30 美元/月。 用量是 Plus 的 4 倍，加入 Grok Bot 、Cursor 云端代理和自动化等功能，获得 X Premium+ 权益。需要这些功能，可以从这一档开始比较。
Super：100 美元/月。 包含 Premium 全部功能，用量是 Plus 的 15 倍，适合先确认较低档用量不够、再考虑升级的用户。
Ultra：200 美元/月。 包含 Super 全部功能，用量是 Plus 的 50 倍，更适合高频使用。它仍有用量上限。
这几个倍数是套餐用量的相对关系，不能换算成固定的对话次数。Grok 、Cursor 以及适用档位的 Grok Bot 会使用同一个每周用量池；在一个产品中消耗较多，留给其他产品的用量也会减少。具体规则可看官方用量说明。
对 Cursor 用户尤其要区分“能选择某个模型”和“会员费已经包含它的用量”。新套餐中，Premium 及以上可以使用 Claude 、GPT 等第三方模型，但从第一次请求起就另行按量计费，不使用套餐包含的周用量； Grok API 也独立计费。Cursor 模型与价格说明列出了这部分规则。
所以，如果主要使用 Grok 和 Cursor 自有模型，再加上 X 权益，联合订阅值得比较；如果主要在 Cursor 里用 Claude 或 GPT ，就要把额外模型费用一起算进去。
已有会员，先核对旧订阅
现有 Cursor 、SuperGrok 、X Premium 用户不必因为新套餐出现就立即重买。官方允许保留旧方案，但切换到联合订阅后，无法恢复旧方案。同时，新套餐不再包含旧 Cursor 套餐中的第三方模型额度；使用这些模型需要另行按量付费。旧 Cursor 套餐与迁移差异
确定迁移后，先按官方账号合并说明核对账号。已有付费 Cursor 的用户，可从 Cursor Unify 进入；不同邮箱可以关联，关键是逐个确认登录的是自己要保留的账号。已有付费 Cursor 账号的迁移界面目前提供 Premium 及以上档位，不能把前面的 Plus 直接当作旧 Pro 的迁移选项。
旧订阅的取消、退款还取决于原付款渠道。例如，通过 Apple 购买的 Cursor 订阅不会随迁移自动取消，需要在 Apple 订阅设置中处理。已有扣款但权益未到账的订单，也应先查原订单，不要再补买一份。
通过 ChongGrok 怎样办理
能够自行完成官方付款的朋友，可以直接查看官方套餐页面。需要支付宝、微信付款，并考虑第三方协助的朋友，我们的入口是：
ChongGrok · X 联合会员开通与套餐说明
ChongGrok 目前提供 Plus 、Premium 、Super 、Ultra 四档月度代订阅。上文列出的是官方美元月价，本站服务价格、订阅周期和交付条件以对应商品页为准。新版兑换需要提交 Grok SSO 登录凭据，它与普通 User ID 不同，不应公开或随意分享。付款前，请先了解需要提交哪些信息，以及通过什么入口提交。旧版 SuperGrok 的充值流程和售后约定，也不能直接套用到联合会员。
办理分三步：
第一步，选择档位，并向页面客服说明自己是否已有 Grok 、Cursor 或 X 付费订阅。
第二步，确认账号是否适用、交付方式、处理时间和售后条件，再进入对应商品页付款。
第三步，取得卡密后，按联合会员兑换页的指引操作。
开通后，分别检查三处
办理结果要在自己的账号里核对：Grok 查看套餐、有效期和用量； Cursor 查看对应账号的可用功能； X 确认关联的个人账号及相应会员权益。X 蓝标和原创内容奖励还各有资格条件，付款并不保证审核通过。
如果订阅没有生效，保留订单号联系售后查询。已经确定需要新版联合会员的朋友，可以在 ChongGrok 联合会员页面查看当前方案，先把账号情况和办理条件确认清楚，再下单。
套餐、价格和服务页面核对日期：2026 年 10 月 19 日。

title: [分享创造] 做了个用 Mac 控制家里所有安卓设备的小工具，手机之间也能互相控制，不走云端（Mac 免费下载 + 安卓内测招募）
summary:
家里抽屉里大概都躺着几台旧安卓：换下来的手机、孩子不用的平板、专门拿来跑某个 App 的备用机。每次想用其中一台，都得先找到它、充上电、解锁、在小屏幕上戳半天。
我想要的很简单：坐在 Mac 前面，家里每一台安卓都在一个窗口里，点开就能看、能用。 找了一圈，要么要登录账号、画面绕一圈云端，要么只能插线用。就自己做了一个，叫「统一控制」（ UnitCtrl ）。

Mac 上能做什么
家里的安卓手机、平板都在左边一列，插线或走 Wi‑Fi 都行，第一次设置好以后就不用线了
实时看画面，鼠标当手指用：点、拖、滚轮翻页；用 Mac 键盘往手机里打字，中文日文都行；手机的声音也能在 Mac 上听
应用管理、文件、截屏录屏，照片直接传进手机相册
每台设备今天亮屏多久、几点开的哪个 App 、存储还剩多少，一眼看到
手机控制手机
在一台手机上打开统一控制，家里其他装了它的设备会一张张列出来，点一下就能看它的屏幕、操作它。帮爸妈弄手机、够一下架子上的旧平板都方便。

几个我比较在意的地方
只在家里的网络里跑：不要账号，不经过云端，我这边也没有任何后台，也就没有什么能被我收集
第一次连要对方点“允许”：没点过允许的设备进不来，允许过的可以在设置里一键全忘掉
不用麦克风和摄像头：传过去的声音只是 App 正在播放的声音
永远没有广告
老实说一句：局域网里的连接目前没有加密，请在自己信任的网络里用
演示视频（ 2 分钟，从打开到远程点一下）： https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ALaN3L4hSbw
下载和内测
Mac 版（免费，macOS 14 起，Apple 芯片和 Intel 都行）： https://github.com/zhaoweijia1997/UnitCtrl/releases 。还没做苹果公证，第一次打开请右键 → 打开。
安卓版在 Google Play 封闭测试里（安卓 10 起）。个人开发者的新账号要凑够 12 人连续测 14 天才能正式上架，愿意帮忙的朋友：
加入测试群组（点“加入群组”就行，不用审批）： https://groups.google.com/g/unitctrl-testers
打开测试链接，点“成为测试人员”： https://play.google.com/apps/testing/app.unitctrl
用同一个账号在 Play 里安装，装着别卸载，留 14 天
代码、界面、四种语言的翻译都是和 Claude 一起写的，我负责出主意和挑毛病。有 bug 、有想法，回帖或者写信 sublueai@gmail.com 都行。谢谢！

title: [推广] 给小店做了个进销存「智存」，一句话录单，欠款、押金、库存分开记
summary:
我做了一款给小店用的进销存，叫「智存」。有 iPhone App ，也有同一店铺共用的网页端，下面把主要用法放在一个帖子里。
拿演示店来讲，一位客户当前欠款 522 元，还有押金 50 元、储值 412 元和 1 只没还的水桶。它们都跟同一个人有关，后面要收的钱、要退的钱和要拿回来的东西却得分别记。智存除了记卖了多少，也把这些往来单独留了记录。
配图都是这间演示店的原生页面。客户和账目是虚构示例，AI 解析页展示的是预置草稿。
说一句或粘贴一段话，先变成可以核对的草稿
比如“林阿姨拿两箱青柠气泡水、三桶桶装水，先挂账”，可以用语音或文字输入，也能把客户发来的订货内容自己粘进来。
先看草稿，再入账。
AI 整理出商品、规格、数量和金额后，你可以逐项改或删，确认好才保存；客户消息需要自己提供，不会读取你的微信聊天。
扫码可以查商品，票据和送货单里的文字也能辅助录入。识别结果都要核对，不能把解析出来的内容直接当成已经记好的账。

正常开单也保留，熟客不用每次从头选货
可以给散客开单，也可以选已有客户。单价、数量、折扣和抹零按这笔生意调整，确认应收金额后，记清实收和挂账。
熟客再次拿货，可以从常买记录里选，也可以点“再来一单”，把已有订单的商品带到新草稿里；价格优先取客户专属价，其次是上次成交价，再用商品标价，落单前仍能改。
单据能分享成图片，客户和供应商也有各自的对账单。

商品按自己卖的东西建
品类、字段、规格可以自定义，也能让 AI 辅助配置行业字段。同一款饮料的不同容量，或者衣服的颜色、尺码，可以分别记价格、成本和库存。批量生成规格时能统一填成本价。
商品可以按名称、编码、条码和规格搜索，散称商品支持小数数量。
1.2.0 里修了一个具体问题。用户有 0.5 斤这样的库存，以前一进盘点页就打不开，现在盘点和退货都补了小数处理；批量建规格时，成本价也能统一填了。

欠款、押金、储值和借出去的物品分开记
客户拿货没付清，欠款跟着订单走；后来分几次还，每次收款也留记录，回到客户页能一起查历史订单、欠款和对账信息。
押金支持收取和退回记录；储值可以记充值、消费和退款，订单结算能使用储值。借出的水桶、周转箱这类物品，也能登记借出、归还和还剩多少没还。
这里记录的是账。
收押金或退款，仍需你通过实际支付方式完成。

进货、供应商欠款和退货接着记
进货单记商品、数量、进价、供应商和已付金额。没有付清的部分留在供应商往来账里，后续付款再补记录；销售退货、进货退货也有各自的处理入口。
销售和进货分别关联库存变化，收付款保留自己的记录，月底可以拿客户或供应商对账单核对。

库存少了，可以回头找是哪一次变动
销售出库、进货入库、盘点和手工调整都会留下流水。点库存变动可以继续查相关单据，缺货时有对应提醒。
盘点时把实盘数量填进去，系统列出盘盈、盘亏，再按实际结果调整。报损、过期等出库也能登记，并按成本记库存损耗开销。


收摊快录、微信账单和报表各管一件事
忙完以后，可以快录一笔营业额，或者把停车、饭钱、摊位费等多笔经营开销一起记下。只记营业额的快录不处理商品库存，要扣具体商品仍需开单。
微信账单使用微信导出的原始 xlsx 文件。店主在网页上传、查重后，再核对哪些款已经记过，手机端可以查看这些导入结果；上传文件本身不计经营收支，也不会把提现一律当成店铺开销。
房租、水电等期间费用可以按期间处理。收支日历看每天的记录，报表看销售、成本、经营费用、商品销售、热销和库存等统计。利润依已录入资料计算，有待核对账单时会提示继续核对。
也有“问生意”入口，可以围绕店里已记录的数据提问；回答和数字仍需回到账目核对。


手机和网页配合用，店员有单独的权限

店主可以导出 CSV 表格或 JSON 备份，数据导出免费。

免费范围、专业版和目前的活动
开单、进货、库存、盘点、对账、收支日历、利润报表和数据导出免费。不订阅也能继续用。

title: [推广] 做了一个免费的视频背景移除工具 CutoutUp，支持 AI 抠像、保留声音、导出透明视频
summary:
大家好，最近独立开发了一个在线视频背景移除工具 CutoutUp，想分享给大家，也希望收集一些真实使用反馈。
网站： https://cutoutup.com/
为什么做这个工具？
之前在处理视频素材时，发现视频抠像比图片抠图麻烦不少。
尤其是想把人物从普通视频中提取出来，放到其他背景上，同时保留原视频声音，并导出真正带透明通道的视频。
不少工具要么需要上传视频到服务器，要么导出格式受限，还有些会丢失音轨。
所以我尝试做了一个直接在浏览器中运行的视频背景移除工具。
目前支持的功能
AI 视频抠像：不需要绿幕，直接去除人物视频背景。
绿幕移除：支持通过色键去除纯色背景，也适用于绿幕拍摄的商品。
视频背景替换：可以将背景换成指定颜色或自己的图片。
GIF 背景移除：支持处理纯色背景的 GIF 动图。
保留原始声音：支持保留视频音轨，避免抠像后变成无声视频。
透明视频导出：支持导出带 Alpha 透明通道的 WebM 视频。
浏览器本地处理：视频不需要上传到服务器，模型和处理过程都在用户设备上运行。
免费额度
目前提供免费使用：
无需注册：每天 3 次任务。
Google 登录：每天总计 6 次免费任务。
免费导出不添加水印。
单段视频目前最长支持 120 秒，导出最高 720p / 30fps 。
对于需要大量处理视频的用户，也提供 $4.99 / 月的不限任务次数方案，按月购买，不自动续费。
目前的一些不足
产品还在持续完善中，也有一些限制：
AI 抠像主要针对人物，复杂背景中的普通物体暂不支持自动识别。
头发、快速运动等复杂边缘可能出现瑕疵。
透明视频目前导出为 WebM ，部分视频编辑软件的兼容性还需要进一步验证。
处理速度依赖本地设备性能，复杂视频可能比较慢。
想收集一些反馈
目前比较想了解几个问题：
大家平时有没有视频抠像的需求？主要用在什么场景？
透明 WebM 是否方便使用？更希望支持哪些导出格式？
本地浏览器处理和云端处理，大家更倾向哪一种？
实际使用中有没有处理失败、速度过慢或者边缘效果不好的情况？
网站上准备了实际处理效果的演示视频，可以先看效果再决定是否尝试。
CutoutUp： https://cutoutup.com/
欢迎体验和提出意见，尤其是功能缺失和兼容性问题，我会持续改进。

title: [生活] 简单的一顿晚餐
summary:
晚上六点下班，到家七点了，坐沙发上看了半天外卖，没想好吃什么，索性翻翻冰箱还有什么东西。
从冰箱拿了一块之前买的肉，还有几根辣椒，就做个辣椒炒肉盖饭吧。

炒完出锅到吃上，历时一个小时，也没觉得太累。
倒了半杯黄酒，边吃边喝，肚子饱了人也微醺，这个状态感到十分满足且幸福。
再玩会游戏,洗澡睡觉。
果然知足者常乐，吃饱喝好，舒服幸福。
兄弟们记得按时吃饭哦。

title: [分享创造] OhMyGame 开源 10 天拿到 936 个 star 的一个小复盘
summary:
我们团队最近开源了一个 AI 游戏创作工具 OhMyGame，主打“开源的一人 AI 游戏工作室”：用户描述自己的想法，Agent 完成游戏设计、生成资产，再进行开发和测试。
我们把 Canvas 和游戏工作流整合在一起，希望让素材生成、编辑和游戏开发的过程更直观。

我们是一个不自带流量的小团队。开源前 10 天，项目拿到了 936 个 star 。想把这段时间的数字、流量来源和用户反馈分享一下，也想请教大家：发布最初一波热度过去后，怎么继续让项目被需要它的人看到？
先说数字
这 10 天里：
936 个 star ，113 个 fork 。
发布了 11 个版本，从 beta.3 到 beta.4.9 。
合并了 131 个 PR 。
用户提了 36 个 issue ，已经关闭了 26 个。
没有投流，主要靠 X 上的内容传播。
下面是这段时间的 star 增长曲线：

查看增长曲线动画
关注从哪里来？
我看了 GitHub 的仓库访问数据，这 10 天总共有 3,648 位访客。前五个访问来源分别是：
X：1,194 位访客。
GitHub 站内：359 位访客。
官网 ohmygame.ai：326 位访客。
Google：208 位访客。
V2EX：138 位访客。
X 一个渠道带来的访客，比后面四个来源加起来还多，占这五个来源合计的约 54%。
这里统计的是仓库访客来源，不是各渠道带来的 star 数，也不是全部访客的来源占比。
比较明显的两次增长，分别发生在两条 X 帖子传播之后。
第一次是开源首发帖。
开源当晚 11 点多，团队成员 Dogxi 发了项目介绍，目前有约 3 万次浏览。
刚发出时没什么动静，第二天早上 7 点左右才开始明显增长，到傍晚新增了大约 300 个 star 。

第二次是 Hyper3D 合作帖。
10 月 10 日晚上，我发了介绍 Hyper3D 合作的帖子，目前有约 2.2 万次浏览。帖子点赞持续增加，第二天仓库又增长了约 180 个 star 。

不过，到了 16 号以后，增长就慢下来了，三天涨了 48 个。
这次比较直接的感受是：至少对我们这个项目来说，外部内容传播带来的关注很明显，GitHub 站内也有流量，但没有自动带来持续增长。
这 10 天，我们怎么回应用户反馈？
我们尽量第一时间回复用户，并尽快修复问题、补上需要的功能。举三个具体例子：
1. 简体中文界面
有人提出需要简体中文界面，3 天后就在 beta.4.7 中上线了。
对应 issue： https://github.com/WhiteTowerAI/ohmygame/issues/134
2. 撤回 Agent 的一轮操作
有人希望 Agent 改坏了之后能退回去。
4 天后发布的 beta.4.9 支持了这个功能：Agent 每轮操作后会列出修改过的文件，用户可以一键撤回。
对应 issue： https://github.com/WhiteTowerAI/ohmygame/issues/202
3. Windows 上的 bug
有人报告示例项目在 Windows 上没法 remix ，37 分钟后修复就合并了，当天随 beta.4.2 发了出去。
对应 issue： https://github.com/WhiteTowerAI/ohmygame/issues/122
目前我们很大一部分开发工作，就是围绕这些真实反馈展开的。
用户已经做出了什么？
贴几个用户作品。下面的图片可以点击，打开对应的实机录屏。
Hunter Space：低多边形风格的 3D 野外探索

Windmere Highlands：在高地草甸和石阵间奔跑

第一人称恐怖走廊，Backrooms 风格

2D 弓箭手放置游戏，带技能树和掉落

为什么做这个？
我自己是 3D 视觉和图形学出身，一直想做和游戏有关的事。
做了前面几个应用之后，我越来越觉得，还是要做自己有感觉的东西。否则遇到困难时，很难一直坚持下去。
选择开源，也是希望大家能用更便宜、更简单的方式创造游戏，和用户一起把工具慢慢做好。
感谢给项目点 star 、提交 issue 和 PR 的朋友，也感谢 Hyper3D 提供赞助，让用户能体验到 3D 生成能力。
接下来
近期我们在研究直接接入 Codex 和 Claude Code 的 CLI ，也会完善互动叙事和插件相关的支持。
更长期还想支持多人游戏、Unity 、Unreal ，以及更多创作工作流。这些还在计划中，需要一步步做。
GitHub： https://github.com/WhiteTowerAI/ohmygame
官网： https://ohmygame.ai
完整博客： https://www.dihuang.me/blog/ohmygame-10-days

title: [旅行] 0 现金， 8807 元，东京\富士山\伊豆\镰仓十日游
summary:
图文版： https://mp.weixin.qq.com/s/gGOCuy1Xco_Ed0n2PP7l2w
国庆，从香港出发去了趟日本
10 天 9 晚，0 现金，全程公共交通，花费 8,807.02 元
出发前，我对日本的认识，大多来自从小到大受到的教育、看过的影视剧，还有后来喜欢的作家村上春树和东野圭吾
临行前，我又读完了 2 本关于日本的书籍：《东京八平米》和《格外的活法》
![1EB9521D-BAC1-44B6-B522-2415A21F8906 1.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/02-1EB9521D-BAC1-44B6-B522-2415A21F8906-1.jpg){: width="600" }
我想了解一个国家，不仅要从书本里，也要从脚印里
这一次是以东京为中心的自由行，除了东京市区，还去了富士山下的河口湖、伊豆大室山和城崎海岸、镰仓
下面记录这十天的行程和感受，也附上费用明细
一、行程总览
连续在横滨住了 8 晚，最后一晚在成田机场，交通主要靠双腿、地铁、大巴
日期

10/2
深圳 → 香港出发 → 羽田机场 → 横滨


10/3
明治神宫 → 涩谷 → 忠犬八公


10/4
上野公园 → 阿美横 → 浅草寺 → 晴空塔周边 → 东京塔

二、十天游记
Day 1 ｜ 10 月 2 日（周五）：凌晨的横滨有点凉
从深圳湾口岸出发，坐巴士前往香港国际机场，匆忙使用信用卡权益在机场的贵宾厅吃了顿晚餐
17:35 起飞，22:55 落地东京羽田机场，时差 1h
![D5EA9148-DC11-41A3-AA0E-B62802DDA8AD_1_102_o.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/04-D5EA9148-DC11-41A3-AA0E-B62802DDA8AD-1-102-o.jpg){: width="600" }
<small style="color:var(--text-muted, #777);">深夜抵达羽田</small>
原以为会赶不上地铁末班车，但是入境、提取行李都比较顺利，提前填写了入境资料卡 VJW ，最后顺利赶上了前往横滨方向的末班车
到达酒店，办理入住，已是 12 点，去 711 便利店买了泡面
坐在路边，一边吃着泡面， 一边吹着风，凌晨的横滨有点凉
Day 2 ｜ 10 月 3 日（周六）：明治神宫、涩谷和忠犬八公
因为睡得太晚，第二天睡到自然醒
吃完午饭，来到东京市区，已是下午 3 点，没有做好任何计划
坐在路边偶遇的一家咖啡店，和 ChatGPT 聊起了行程规划，决定第一站去明治神宫
![CCE4ED83-15D1-4C5E-865C-78366C6CA3EE_1_102_o.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/05-CCE4ED83-15D1-4C5E-865C-78366C6CA3EE-1-102-o.jpg){: width="340" }
<small style="color:var(--text-muted, #777);">街边咖啡店</small>
这座神社位于原宿附近，周围有大片树林和安静的步道，相比热闹的东京商业区，这里显得安静而又有灵性，绿树蔽日
![3CD28C37-8284-4C7D-8048-04E3DAC73EAE_1_105_c.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/06-3CD28C37-8284-4C7D-8048-04E3DAC73EAE-1-105-c.jpg){: width="360" }
<small style="color:var(--text-muted, #777);">明治神宫，门内门外</small>
神社前，挂满了祈福的木板，无论是英文、日语、韩语，还是中文，大家的心愿不外乎都是“工作、健康、爱情、财富...”
![3127BC08-2365-4FD4-95E6-D2EB0CE0F346_1_105_c.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/07-3127BC08-2365-4FD4-95E6-D2EB0CE0F346-1-105-c.jpg){: width="360" }
<small style="color:var(--text-muted, #777);">心愿</small>
走出明治神宫，便是原宿站步行街，初秋的东京，风也是凉爽的
![934B6733-6AD6-4ACE-A62E-DABF3D5CB640_1_102_o.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/08-934B6733-6AD6-4ACE-A62E-DABF3D5CB640-1-102-o.jpg){: width="360" }
随后去了涩谷，这里有著名的涩谷十字路口，繁忙的街区、五颜六色的霓虹灯，还有绿灯亮起便冲到马路上自拍的各国友人

<small style="color:var(--text-muted, #777);">涩谷的夜色与人流</small>
在马路的角落，挤满了人，走近一看，是忠犬八公雕像
![66316469-311B-4637-93A4-183EA2E8FE28_1_102_o 1.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/10-66316469-311B-4637-93A4-183EA2E8FE28-1-102-o-1.jpg){: width="340" }
我翻开豆瓣，2020-05-24 标记看过，4 星

Day 3 ｜ 10 月 4 日（周日）：从上野公园走到东京塔
这是东京市区游览内容最丰富的一天
上野公园与阿美横
漫步在上野恩赐公园，到处是淡雅的桂花香
不到几百米，就有 2 波街头艺人表演
一个小姑娘，站在人群第一排，不停的鼓掌呐喊加油，最后被邀请一起表演杂技，抓拍到了下面这张
![99D05468-6EC7-4422-AC71-B7F2673B19A3_1_105_c.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/12-99D05468-6EC7-4422-AC71-B7F2673B19A3-1-105-c.jpg){: width="384" } ![3BB73426-3709-409F-93B9-013DAA7C5CC4_1_105_c.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/13-3BB73426-3709-409F-93B9-013DAA7C5CC4-1-105-c.jpg){: width="216" }
<small style="color:var(--text-muted, #777);">从台下鼓掌，到一起参与表演</small>
不忍池其实是一个小湖泊，微风拂面，不少人在此划船，这画面像是上个世纪末的电影
![753C916D-A399-49B2-AF32-B2D54DF106E6_1_105_c.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/14-753C916D-A399-49B2-AF32-B2D54DF106E6-1-105-c.jpg){: width="640" }
<small style="color:var(--text-muted, #777);">不忍池，划船的人与天鹅船</small>
走出上野公园，步行 15 分钟，就是阿美横商店街，本地海鲜菜市场、小吃、食品、日用品和各类商铺，可以感受本地人的日常，也顺便解决午餐
![AD09A438-8D92-4543-B34B-AC867E9BDA19_1_102_o.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/15-AD09A438-8D92-4543-B34B-AC867E9BDA19-1-102-o.jpg){: width="360" }
<small style="color:var(--text-muted, #777);">阿美横，热闹的商店街</small>
小说里认识的浅草寺
从上野坐地铁来到浅草，走出地铁站，经过雷门和仲见世商店街
感觉这里像是国内景区的商业街，都是些毫无质感和特色的商品
穿过商业街，浮现在眼前的就是浅草寺
夕阳打在“浅草寺”这三个字上，突然想起以前在东野圭吾《时生》中读到的情节
![628941AD-485D-4D03-A0AB-AC207128B84A_1_102_o.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/16-628941AD-485D-4D03-A0AB-AC207128B84A-1-102-o.jpg){: width="300" } ![66539B20-505D-44E0-9895-6E54AEBC9EF2_1_102_o.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/17-66539B20-505D-44E0-9895-6E54AEBC9EF2-1-102-o.jpg){: width="300" }
<small style="color:var(--text-muted, #777);">浅草寺的人潮，与夕阳里的牌匾</small>
第一次来到这里，现实中的地方却早已在小说中认识，有种奇妙的熟悉感
本想在寺庙买一点纪念品，发现不支持信用卡，想找人临时兑换，都被拒绝了，索性放弃
晴空塔与东京塔
参观浅草寺后，步行 10 分钟，便是隅田川
夜色初上，对岸的晴空塔逐渐点亮，通明的列车驶过河面，不少人在慢跑
![4A40D009-8298-425B-91CB-E88FA120E4A5_1_105_c.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/18-4A40D009-8298-425B-91CB-E88FA120E4A5-1-105-c.jpg){: width="216" } ![4D2744A9-A4C9-416C-99EF-A3E3C134AF13_1_102_o.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/19-4D2744A9-A4C9-416C-99EF-A3E3C134AF13-1-102-o.jpg){: width="384" }
<small style="color:var(--text-muted, #777);">隅田川边，晴空塔与驶过河面的列车</small>
晚上，乘坐地铁到大门站，街边拐角，抬头就是东京塔
![8B9945AC-2DCF-4AF8-85E2-9642B30E017C_1_102_o.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/20-8B9945AC-2DCF-4AF8-85E2-9642B30E017C-1-102-o.jpg){: width="380" }
买了一张 1500 日元的门票，登上了 150 米主展望台 Main Deck
站在高处欣赏东京密集的城市灯光，说实话，超级城市的夜景都大同小异
![DA61436C-1A6F-478F-A46D-ACBAF091DB57_1_102_o.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/21-DA61436C-1A6F-478F-A46D-ACBAF091DB57-1-102-o.jpg){: width="640" }
<small style="color:var(--text-muted, #777);">东京塔上看到的城市夜景</small>
东京塔更适合站在塔下，或者远观
Day 4 ｜ 10 月 5 日（周一）：筑地、银座、东京站和秋叶原
当天出门时天气不太好，下起了雨，但打伞的人不多
来到筑地场外市场，是一条海鲜街，还有刀具店，基本上都是欧美的游客，整体感觉一般
![79CA3949-4EA1-40FE-8045-ED2DE6A62064_1_102_o.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/22-79CA3949-4EA1-40FE-8045-ED2DE6A62064-1-102-o.jpg){: width="640" }
<small style="color:var(--text-muted, #777);">筑地场外市场，摊位上的海鲜</small>
从筑地到银座距离不远，经过银座四丁目，可以看到和光钟楼、中央通及各类奢侈品牌
![64382318-484B-4DBF-8E28-710403E385B1_1_102_o.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/23-64382318-484B-4DBF-8E28-710403E385B1-1-102-o.jpg){: width="340" }
<small style="color:var(--text-muted, #777);">银座和光钟楼</small>
当天一个非常重要的目的地，是东京站
因为提前网上购买了第二天 08:10 前往富士山河口湖的大巴票，需要提前踩点，东京站真的太大了，有点类似深圳北，但是更有秩序感
询问工作人员，很容易就找到了第二天的 JR 高速巴士乘车处
解决了心头大患，随机走进路边咖啡店“椿屋咖啡”，价格贵，味道一般，除了环境好，买单之后，对星巴克的好感+1
![FC31D9F3-E169-4D16-AD29-FB4A43D76876_1_102_o.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/24-FC31D9F3-E169-4D16-AD29-FB4A43D76876-1-102-o.jpg){: width="320" }
<small style="color:var(--text-muted, #777);">椿屋咖啡</small>
随后去了秋叶原，除了电子产品、动漫、游戏，这里还有很多大型的成人用品商店，比如「大人のデパート M’s 」
![69100312-F30D-4FDB-9F77-5E6FE4E123B7_1_102_o.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/25-69100312-F30D-4FDB-9F77-5E6FE4E123B7-1-102-o.jpg){: width="320" }
<small style="color:var(--text-muted, #777);">秋叶原街头</small>
随便逛了逛，大受震惊，出来的时候，在狭小的电梯里，进来了一对中国情侣，购物篮里装满了不可描述的物品
Day 5 ｜ 10 月 6 日（周二）：没等到富士山，沿着河口湖走了回去
早晨从鹤见出发，到东京站乘坐 08:10 的大巴，前往河口湖
抵达河口湖后，发现云层非常厚，坐观光巴士到终点站：河口湖自然生活馆，本来是看富士山的好地方，但当天一直没能看到完整山体
![C4EC002E-1119-4997-946A-209AD9709581_1_102_o.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/26-C4EC002E-1119-4997-946A-209AD9709581-1-102-o.jpg){: width="343" } ![9FA90FFE-F11B-481E-A05D-D2255AB44301_1_102_o.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/27-9FA90FFE-F11B-481E-A05D-D2255AB44301-1-102-o.jpg){: width="257" }
<small style="color:var(--text-muted, #777);">初到河口湖，湖边的骑行人与窗外的风景</small>
午餐之后，坐在湖边餐厅的二楼，希望云层慢慢散去，一直到下午 3 点才选择了放弃
![7301757F-806E-4F21-8651-01419A86EA8D_1_102_o.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/28-7301757F-806E-4F21-8651-01419A86EA8D-1-102-o.jpg){: width="200" } ![CBA30285-882B-4566-9D09-EA10C543B9A3_1_102_o.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/29-CBA30285-882B-4566-9D09-EA10C543B9A3-1-102-o.jpg){: width="400" }
<small style="color:var(--text-muted, #777);">云中富士山，和餐厅二楼窗外的河口湖</small>
周边有一些小商店，一款手工冰箱贴，价格约 1980 日元，忍住了没有购买
![D5F0281F-724C-4F01-B272-87A5F006F9B5_1_102_o.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/30-D5F0281F-724C-4F01-B272-87A5F006F9B5-1-102-o.jpg){: width="300" } 
<small style="color:var(--text-muted, #777);">1980 日元的冰箱贴</small>
没有乘坐观光巴士返回河口湖站，而是沿着河口湖岸徒步，这是当天最意外的收获
从天亮走到天黑，沿途没什么游客，偶尔遇到几个跑步或者骑行的人
![205270D1-4A60-421E-B2DA-F035BD281A4C_1_102_o.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/31-205270D1-4A60-421E-B2DA-F035BD281A4C-1-102-o.jpg){: width="280" } ![471F8C15-5598-4DF1-823F-8E6327B4F8CD_1_102_o.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/32-471F8C15-5598-4DF1-823F-8E6327B4F8CD-1-102-o.jpg){: width="280" }
<small style="color:var(--text-muted, #777);">沿湖走回车站，路上的骑行人与傍晚的步道</small>
虽然没看到完整的富士山，但这段沿湖的绿道还是让人流连忘返
回到河口湖站，不到 6 点，而晚上返回东京的大巴是 19:30
![9B7A4C34-58EF-4DBB-891C-687AE1280241_1_102_o.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/33-9B7A4C34-58EF-4DBB-891C-687AE1280241-1-102-o.jpg){: width="200" } ![DEF1886F-C9AD-443A-9BC0-DB33FC6476C8_1_102_o.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/34-DEF1886F-C9AD-443A-9BC0-DB33FC6476C8-1-102-o.jpg){: width="400" }
<small style="color:var(--text-muted, #777);">回程路上的邮筒，与河口湖的暮色</small>
如果下次再去的话，我会选择在河口湖住一晚，更深度的体验
Day 6 ｜ 10 月 7 日（周三）：惠比寿、目黑，以及一家烧鸟店
此前几天走得比较多，所以决定在东京放松一天
惠比寿有很多有特色的餐具和艺术品商店，目黑区散落着各种街头咖啡店
![1EE30872-887B-49A5-89AD-3874ECA4284C_1_102_o.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/35-1EE30872-887B-49A5-89AD-3874ECA4284C-1-102-o.jpg){: width="185" } ![214C8979-1520-4769-A4CF-D24029B1330A_1_102_o.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/36-214C8979-1520-4769-A4CF-D24029B1330A-1-102-o.jpg){: width="415" }
<small style="color:var(--text-muted, #777);">小店里的植物与餐具</small>
![2B80F0D7-5F4F-44EB-861C-6353318F01E7_1_102_o.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/37-2B80F0D7-5F4F-44EB-861C-6353318F01E7-1-102-o.jpg){: width="520" }
<small style="color:var(--text-muted, #777);">认真打包的店员</small>
在惠比寿花园广场一楼的星巴克点了一杯咖啡，乘坐旁边的电梯到 33 楼，可以免费从空中观赏东京塔，和夜晚又是不一样的感受
![2843F09D-7CD7-4A5A-B6AD-B10C0C3669E3_1_102_o 1.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/38-2843F09D-7CD7-4A5A-B6AD-B10C0C3669E3-1-102-o-1.jpg){: width="340" }
<small style="color:var(--text-muted, #777);">白天，从高处远望东京塔</small>
傍晚散步来到了星巴克臻选东京烘焙工坊，这是星巴克全球第五家（继西雅图、上海、米兰、纽约之后），总共 4 层，星巴克爱好者可以打卡
![8973AEA1-627D-41EB-92ED-94B51CDF1D99_1_102_o.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/39-8973AEA1-627D-41EB-92ED-94B51CDF1D99-1-102-o.jpg){: width="185" } ![E8E0F05B-2C8C-475A-AF3A-908C2D81BE8B_1_102_o.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/40-E8E0F05B-2C8C-475A-AF3A-908C2D81BE8B-1-102-o.jpg){: width="415" }
<small style="color:var(--text-muted, #777);">东京烘焙工坊，铜色设备与整面杯子墙</small>
意外走进一家当地烧鸟店
晚上已经吃过晚饭，路过一家坐满人的烧鸟店，原本只是站在门外拍照
![C28EFD0A-ADBA-4430-89C9-9A7EF2BF3ABE_1_102_o.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/41-C28EFD0A-ADBA-4430-89C9-9A7EF2BF3ABE-1-102-o.jpg){: width="640" }
一位刚从餐厅吃完饭的陌生人主动询问我们是不是游客，并建议进去体验当地特色
餐厅没有英文菜单，于是借助 AI 点菜
![B61E5B70-7505-4554-9CD8-5CD31684F8CF_1_102_o.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/42-B61E5B70-7505-4554-9CD8-5CD31684F8CF-1-102-o.jpg){: width="640" }
<small style="color:var(--text-muted, #777);">吧台里的烟火气</small>
点餐时，左边的年轻人打开 Google 翻译，热心的帮忙推荐
买单时，右边原本背对着我们的女生，主动帮忙翻译
离开时，斜对面的一对夫妇朝我们微笑，挥手告别
Day 7 ｜ 10 月 8 日（周四）：在大室山，意外看到了富士山
调整一天后，开启了伊豆之行，这是整趟旅行里换乘最复杂的一天
早晨 6 点多从酒店出发，从鹤见到横滨，经过热海，再到伊豆高原，换乘巴士前往大室山
从热海到伊豆这一段，列车行驶在海岸线旁边，对面的乘客在看书，阳光打在他的身上，真希望这列火车可以一直开下去...
![9203F2AC-106F-464D-AAA9-AB4B934218B3_1_105_c.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/43-9203F2AC-106F-464D-AAA9-AB4B934218B3-1-105-c.jpg){: width="640" }
大室山是一座火山锥，可以乘坐登山缆车上山，往返价格才 1000 日元
![949395C0-269F-4E64-B2F5-EE30CB779D12_1_102_o.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/44-949395C0-269F-4E64-B2F5-EE30CB779D12-1-102-o.jpg){: width="640" }
前两天在河口湖没能看到完整山体，但在大室山，却意外看到了远处的富士山，这算是旅途中的惊喜
![4D144617-CBE8-4A7C-85A0-25C418BD48F5_1_102_o.jpeg](/img/article-studio/2026-10-19-0 现金-8807 元-日本国庆十日游/45-4D144617-CBE8-4A7C-85A0-25C418BD48F5-1-102-o.jpg){: width="640" }
山顶火山口步道约 1 公里，走走停停，逗留了 2 个小时

title:
[分享创造] 为了不让闲置的备案被管局注销,索性单搓了个 macOS 侧边栏笔记： iFolo Note
, macOS 侧边栏简约笔记
summary:
前阵子让 muse 整理云资产，发现早年藏箱子底的项目 https://www.ifolo.cn 和辛苦拿下的 ICP 备案号一直在吃灰,还有 claude 的 tokens,索性拯救了一下尸山代码,搓了一个 macOS 侧边栏笔记：iFolo Note.按我自己使用习惯来的,大家可酌情使用,可提提意见!免费,免费,免费!
为什么要造这个轮子？
每天面对 IDE 和 多 Agent 终端，我在 Mac 上随手记东西一直很割裂：
重型软件太重：只是想临时贴段 JSON 、记行命令或闪念，用 Notion 、Obsidian 甚至系统备忘录都得 Cmd + Tab 切窗口，打断思路。
桌面便签太乱：贴多了像牛皮癣，过后根本找不到。
我想要的只是一个平时完全隐形、需要时从屏幕边缘一秒滑出、写完立刻缩回去,AI 时代还支持可控 mcp的轻量容器。
核心特点
无感边缘呼出：常驻屏幕侧边，鼠标贴边或快捷键秒开。全屏写代码、开会时随叫随到，不抢焦点，用完即走。
原生丝滑体验：拒绝套壳卡顿，深度优化了滑出帧率与输入延迟，后台常驻几乎零感。
Markdown 混排直出：代码片段、Todo 、临时链接所见即所得，无需在源码和预览模式间反复横跳。
不只是临时草稿：支持双链与标签整理，纯本地 Markdown 存储,目前还没做云端同步、s
3 同步啥的，Mac 侧边栏记下的碎片灵感，随时能在 iOS 端继续整理，数据完全自主。





目前 Macos 端已稳定,后期计划 windows 端，欢迎大家体验,免费、免费!：
👉 官网： https://www.ifolo.cn

title: [PHP] DuckPhp 1.4.1 发布
summary:
把两个现成的应用塞进一个跑了八年的老站点——DuckPHP 的多应用互嵌 本文所有输出都是在本机（ PHP 8.2 + DuckPHP 1.4.1 ）实跑得到的结果，代码可以照着抄。 先说场景 你手上有一个跑了八年的老站点：一堆 PHP 脚本、静态页、可能还有别人写的小工具。现在要加三样东西： 一个后台管理界面； 一个内部博客； 一个给 App 用的 API 。 常见的路数是"上框架"——然后你发现：要把整个站点搬进它的目录结构，要改 nginx 的 rewrite ，要把老代码改造成它的控制器，还得祈祷它和站点里那套老 Session/老 DB 封装不打架。八年的东西，动一下就有人半夜打电话给你。 DuckPHP 走的是另一条路：它不要求你搬家，它自己搬进来。 先看结果 我在本地搭了个"老站点"，document_root 下只有一个静态页和新建的 app/ 目录： legacy-site/ ← 老站点，document_root 指向这里 ├── index.html ← 跑了八年的老页面（纯静态） └── app/ ← 新加的 DuckPHP 应用 ├── index.php ← 唯一入口 ├── blog/BlogApp.php └── shop/ShopApp.php 启动服务（php -S 127.0.0.1:8099 -t legacy-site），三个请求： $ curl http://127.0.0.1:8099/ 老站点

我是跑了八年的老站点

$ curl http://127.0.0.1:8099/app/index.php HOST: blog | shop $ curl "http://127.0.0.1:8099/app/index.php?_r=blog%2Findex" [blog] path=/tmp/legacy/app/blog/ [blog] url=/app/index.php 注意三件事： 老站点原样活着，/ 还是那个静态页； 新应用就挂在 /app/ 下，没有改任何 rewrite 配置； blog 和 shop 是两个独立的 DuckPHP 应用，各自有各自的 path（/tmp/legacy/app/blog/ 和 /tmp/legacy/app/shop/），只是被同一个入口挂到了 /app/index.php?_r=blog/... 和 ?_r=shop/... 上。 上面输出里 path= 后面的绝对路径随你本机的目录而定。 它是怎么做到的 一个入口，一个 app 数组 app/index.php 就是全部（下面这段我实跑通过）： __DIR__, 'controller_welcome_class' => SiteApp::class, 'app' => [ // ← 登记子应用 \Blog\BlogApp::class => [ 'name' => 'blog', 'controller_url_prefix' => 'blog/', // URL 空间：/blog/ ], \Shop\ShopApp::class => [ 'name' => 'shop', 'controller_url_prefix' => 'shop/', // URL 空间：/shop/ ], ], ]; public function action_index() { echo 'HOST: blog' . ' | shop'; } } SiteApp::RunQuickly([]); 子应用是自己声明自己的普通应用类，父应用不碰它的内部： __DIR__, // 它自己的根：视图/配置/控制器都从这里找 'namespace' => 'Blog', // 它自己的命名空间 'controller_welcome_class' => BlogApp::class, ]; public function action_index() { echo '[blog] path=' . static::_()->options['path'] . "\n"; echo '[blog] url=' . __url('') . "\n"; } } shop/ShopApp.php 同理，只是 path 指向 shop/、前缀是 shop/。 两个关键点 path 管"文件从哪找"，controller_url_prefix 管"URL 从哪开始匹配"。 前者决定子应用的视图、配置、控制器目录（所以两个子应用可以各带各的目录树，互不干扰）；后者决定谁接管哪段 URL 。两者是分开的，所以你既能"子目录部署"（path 不变、前缀加目录名），也能"平铺挂载"（前缀就是应用名）。 不需要 PATH_INFO 。 无 PATH_INFO 路由是默认开启的：RouteHookPathInfoCompat 的 path_info_compact_enable 默认为 true ，所以 URL 里带的是 ?_r=（想要常规 PATH_INFO 就把它设成 false）。这带来一个很实际的好处：老站点的 nginx/Apache 配置一行都不用改——你只要把新应用放到 document_root 下的某个目录、入口文件能被访问到，剩下的都归框架管。"不改配置"是它能在老项目里落地的关键。 底下是"相位（ Phase ）" 父子应用不是简单的 require 拼在一起：框架给每个应用一个相位，装配、单例、异常处理都在各自相位里完成。所以父应用换了 View 实现，子应用不受影响；子应用自己的 path、namespace、CLI 命令前缀也都是独立的。上面输出里两个子应用各自打出自己的 path，就是这件事最直接的证据。 这件事为什么值得单独说 大多数框架的"模块化"是代码层面的：一个目录、一个命名空间、一个服务提供者。DuckPHP 的互嵌是应用层面的： 别人的应用可以直接挂进来。同事写的、从 vendor/ 装的 DuckPHP 应用，只要类能被加载（ composer 包连 autoload 都不用管），登记到 app 数组里就是一个子应用。框架自己的 E2E 测试（tests/data_for_tests/ZThirdDemo + tests/ZThirdDemoTest.php）就是拿"主应用 + third/ 里的第三方应用"这么跑的。 老项目可以渐进式改造。先在 /app/ 挂一个小应用跑通，再一个模块一个模块往里搬；老代码一行不动，回滚就是删一个目录。 **一个域名下可以有多个"独立应用"**。博客、后台、API 各自一套目录和配置，各自能跑自己的 CLI 命令（带相位前缀），需要时还能用独立数据库连接（local_database），但对外只是一个站点。 测试友好。子应用能单独起、单独测，也能在父应用里做集成测试。 想要现成的后台和用户系统？可以接 DuckAdmin DuckPHP 本体只提供机制（GlobalUser / GlobalAdmin 及其 Controller 骨架类）；现成的管理后台 + 用户系统由同作者的 Composer 包 dvaknheo/duckadmin 提供： composer require dvaknheo/duckadmin 它本身就是一个 DuckPHP 应用，可以按上一节的方式当成子应用挂进来；具体用法以 DuckAdmin 的文档为准。 注：DuckAdmin 要到稍后的版本才会稳定，这一节没有实测——先了解，别急着上生产。 顺手说几句它的底色 零依赖：composer require dvaknheo/duckphp，require 里只有 php >= 7.4，依赖树里不会多出一堆传递依赖。 库模式：它是你项目的一个依赖，不是"你得搬进它的骨架"。骨架工程（./vendor/bin/duckphp new）是可选的。 全组件可替换：View、Cache、DbManager、Logger……都是可变单例，老项目里已经有一套封装时，换装配就行，业务代码不动。 不造抽象：不做模板引擎（ PHP 就是模板）、不做 ORM （ PDO 薄封装，SQL 在日志里看得见）、不套中间件栈（堆栈清晰，出错好查）。 质量：95 个测试用例、892 个断言、src/ 行覆盖率 100%（ 4737/4737 ）；文档 47 章用户指南 + 112 篇参考手册，中英双语。 什么情况下别用它 你要的是开箱即用的后台管理 + CRUD 生成器——它给的是机制，业务自己写； 你需要庞大的中间件生态（队列、限流、验证器全家桶）——它不是这个路线； 试一下 composer require dvaknheo/duckphp ./vendor/bin/duckphp new # 可选：生成骨架工程 Gitee：https://gitee.com/dvaknheo/duckphp GitHub：https://github.com/dvaknheo/duckphp 文档：仓库内 docs/zh/index.md（中文）、docs/en/（英文） 版本：Packagist 上 dvaknheo/duckphp 1.4.1

title: [程序员] zcode 非官方手机端，有兴趣的捧个场
summary:
四台机器，一个页面，零次切窗。
我有四台机器在跑 ZCode：公司台式、家里笔记本、云主机、Mac mini。
以前最烦的不是看不到进度，而是看不过来。每台机器一个窗口，切来切去，上下文全断。想看眼 e2e、批个权限、补一句 prompt，得先把窗口找出来。
所以我写了个 Android 客户端。做完才发现，手机扫码只是入口，真正解决问题的是多机聚合：
手机扫码，一次绑定多台桌面；
手机本地起一个群控台 Web 服务；
同一 Wi-Fi 下，PC 浏览器打开这个地址；
每台机器一个独立会话，单屏 / 双列 / 四宫格随便切；
PC 直连官方云，不经过手机转发。页面不关，就能一直连着多台机器。
现在的日常：早上到公司，四台机器同屏。
左上：办公室 MacBook 在重构登录模块
右上：家里台式机在跑全量 e2e
左下：云主机在部署 staging
右下：Mac mini 在等我看 PR #42
不用 Cmd+Tab，也不用给每台机器开一个远程桌面。它不是远程桌面，只是把官方会话页聚合成一个多机控制台。
技术实现也很直接：WebView 承载官方手机页，扫码或通过深链接绑定，凭据只存本机，https + 官方域名白名单 + sid/hash 校验；群控台本质上就是把凭据下发给浏览器，让 PC 自己连官方云。
手机端本身也能单独扫码接管，通勤、出门、躺床上都能看进度、批权限、补 prompt。
适合同时开多台开发机、多环境跑 Agent 的人；只有一台机器的话，手机端扫码接管也够用。
非官方客户端，Android 8.0+，APK 5.7 MB，直接装。debug 签名，内测/自用没问题，别拿去上架。 代码在 GitHub / Gitee，欢迎 Issue / PR。
GitHub： https://github.com/woshihoujinxin/zcode-mobile-android 
Gitee： https://gitee.com/houjinxin/zcode-mobile-android
最近 GLM 降智严重，大家可以在本地配置好别的模型，推荐 DS

所以现状就是用完 claude pro 之后用 gpt plus ，然后等苹果把我 apple id 解锁之后再次尝试升级到 max 5x ，看看到时候会不会出现手机号验证或 kyc

真实付款下单那一步还没完整跑过，字段照文档写的，有坑再修。
演示活动一直开着，填个名字能看到自己在名单里，不会真开奖。

title: [分享创造] 上岸线：上线国考选岗工具后，被用户一句话问住了： 230 个岗位你让我猜？
summary:
前段时间我上线了「上岸线」，一个国考职位分数线查询和智能选岗工具：
https://shanganxian.cn/
本来我自我感觉良好：
专业能筛，学历能筛，政治面貌能筛，基层年限能筛，地区能筛，分数还能分“冲 / 稳 / 保”。
结果用户一句话把我问住了：
“输入了所有条件后，可以看到有 230 个岗位，看不到具体的岗位，提示结果超过 200 个，说明条件还不够明确。然而所有限制条件都选上了，又没有其他限制条件了。”
我看完沉默了三秒。
用户的条件已经填完了，我却告诉他：“你的条件不够明确，所以我不给你看结果。”
这逻辑确实有点像：
“你已经把身份证、准考证、学历证书都拿出来了。但我还是觉得你不够像本人。”
所以这轮更新，主要就是把这种不太像话的地方改了。
结果终于能看了
以前超过 200 个结果，就提示“条件不够明确”，
现在不了。
230 个岗位就老老实实给你看 230 个。只有结果 前 500 个，防止页面卡成 PPT 。
筛选工具的第一要义：别把筛选结果藏起来。
新增“应届限制”
现在可以选：
只看限应届岗位
排除限应届岗位
比如职位备注里写了“限应届高校毕业生报考”“仅  会被识别出来。
之前这个条件没做，导致用户把能选的都选完了，
新增“毕业身份”
现在可以选：
当年应届（ 2027 届）
择业期应届（ 2025 / 2026 届，未落实工作）
往届 / 非应届
择业期应届会排除“仅限 2027 年应届”的岗位；往届 / 非应届会排除限应届岗位。
简单说，就是让系统先搞清楚你属于哪一类，而不玩文字推理。
当然，最终资格还是以当年报考指南和招录机关审拍胸脯。
修正了一个容易误解的文案
以前“基层工作年限”里有个选项叫“无 / 应届”。
这个写法确实容易让人误会：没有基层工作年限要
一个管你有没有工作经历，一个管你是不是应届，不能强行拜把子。
现在改成了：
“无基层工作经历要求”
放了一份免费国考资料
首页现在有个「国考资料（网盘）」入口，可以领取试题资料等，免费转存：
https://shanganxian.cn/go/netdisk/?from=v2ex
不用付款，不用砍价。
这个站目前还在早期。数据来自国家公务员局公开 线只是参考，报考还是要以官方公告、职位表备注和招录机关解释为准。
如果你最近也在看 2027 国考岗位，可以试一下。
觉得好用可以不说，觉得难用最好说一下。如果能顺便带上职位代码，那就更好了，我改起来能少猜一点。

title: Structured Authority Injection: Persistent Human Control for LLM Agents via Typed MCP Overrides
summary:
arXiv:2610.22373v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM-based agents are increasingly used as autonomous orchestrators in distributed and multi-agent systems, yet a control gap remains: no protocol-level mechanism allows human operators to inject binding directives that persist across planning cycles. Free-text overrides suffer from ambiguous interpretation due to lack of schema validation and from authority erosion as operator instructions lose influence within accumulating context. We propose Structured Authority Injection (SAI), a protocol that addresses these issues by routing operator corrections through typed, schema-validated Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool calls and maintaining a ranked authority context prepended to each LLM prompt. SAI defines three override classes (Constraint, Priority, and Strategy) with distinct persistence semantics and an explicit precedence order enforced via a directed authority channel inaccessible to the planning process. The method requires no model fine-tuning or access to model weights and applies to instruction-tuned LLMs supporting MCP tool use. Evaluation across nine LLMs and eight scenarios targeting agent failure modes shows reduced ambiguous directive interpretation and mitigated authority decay across planning iterations, with lower prompt overhead in the strongest models (up to 38% depending on model and scenario), though benefit varies substantially across models. SAI provides a general design pattern for agent systems requiring explicit and persistent human control.

title: Rethinking User Encoders: Routing Diffusion States for Scenario-Adaptive User Representation
summary:
arXiv:2610.22400v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Existing large language model (LLM)-based user encoders serialize heterogeneous behavioral logs and compress them into static representations through autoregressive (AR) prediction. However, their unidirectional constraint limits bidirectional information flow, hindering cross-modal interactions and the joint preservation of multi-source signals. Consequently, the learned static representations struggle to accommodate the distinct evidence requirements of diverse downstream scenarios. We address these limitations by unlocking the iterative denoising process of diffusion language models (dLLMs) as a multi-granularity reconstruction space. Based on this insight, we propose FINDERS (FactorIzatioN of Diffusion statEs for Routing across Scenarios), a router-equipped dLLM framework comprising four operations: denoise, factorize, route, and compress. Learnable meta-slots organize complementary denoising states into transferable cross-modal semantics and modality-specific behavioral factors. To provide grounded supervision, we construct BehaviorQA, a large-scale corpus containing explicit behavioral rationales. Guided by scenario queries, a lightweight router dynamically emphasizes relevant slot directions via an input-level residual pathway before cross-source fusion and final compression. Extensive experiments and online A/B tests across ten industrial scenarios demonstrate that FINDERS consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both unified and scenario-adaptive settings. This work effectively pushes the boundaries of dLLMs beyond language generation, demonstrating their immense potential as powerful user representation learners.

title: From Events to Reasoning: Hierarchical Rule Composition over Explicit States
summary:
arXiv:2610.22403v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: What a reasoning system emits is a conclusion; what it owes is a justification. Producing one requires every operation to be admissible on the facts actually available, the dependencies of intermediate results to survive to the end of the path, and the path to be revised when a premise changes. We present the Event Reasoning System (ERS), in which the reasoning state is an explicit event graph. Semantic features nominate candidate objects and rule bindings, and declared rule and task conditions decide which may execute, so candidates that violate the represented period, unit, or evidence constraints cannot enter an accepted reasoning path. Low-level rules provide reusable local transformations, and recursively composable high-level control rules organize subgoals and legal paths under the current goal, information gaps, and budget; a finite library is thereby rebound into paths never stored as complete solutions. We formalize admissible transitions, task-dependent control, compositional expressivity, dependency-preserving revision, and the gap between reachable solutions and those a budgeted controller finds. On structured-event graphs, ERS builds dependency chains of up to twelve steps, cuts irrelevant executed domain operations from 32 to 0 as lookahead grows to 16, and produces no unsupported target output across 24 negative cases; with rules frozen, it passes 12/12 focused checks comprising nine accepted derivations involving unseen input/path combinations and three justified refusals, as well as 6/6 fact-change cases. On fourteen jointly solved development tasks, the recorded dynamic subgoal configuration uses 51.6% less inference wall-clock time than single-level global control under their respective frozen settings.

title: ECHOES: Seeing Beyond the Current Image via Recursive History Compression and Privileged On-Policy Distillation
summary:
arXiv:2610.22408v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-horizon GUI agents rely on visual history to maintain task states, but retaining historical screenshots increases visual-token usage and inference costs, while textual summaries can discard critical state information, undermining long-horizon reliability. We propose ECHOES, which leverages training-time privileged information to guide textual history compression and strengthen long-horizon reasoning. Specifically, ECHOES adopts a Compression-Think-Action (CTA) format to recursively update a textual history state and reason. The same model, given privileged multi-image inputs, serves as a teacher that provides dense token-level on-policy distillation on student-generated CTA rollouts. Our Perception-Memory Fidelity (PMF) Gap-guided OPD-RL framework dynamically balances privileged distillation and task-reward optimization, with periodic teacher updates supporting continued improvement. We further introduce ECHOESBMK, a fine-grained diagnostic benchmark derived from real GUI agent failure trajectories to jointly evaluate visual perception and cross-modal state retention. Experiments on four GUI benchmarks and ECHOESBMK demonstrate substantial gains in task performance and memory fidelity. Without retaining historical screenshots at deployment, ECHOES achieves competitive performance with a favorable performance-inference-cost trade-off and exhibits positive zero-shot transfer to unseen visual planning tasks.

title: Sensitivity Analysis of Decision Rules in an Agent-Based Agro-Ecological Model
summary:
arXiv:2610.22420v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Agent-based models are well-suited for modelling agro-ecological systems for decision-making, yet turning their simulations into actionable insight requires identifying which decisions actually drive the behaviours. In such a context, sensitivity analysis stumbles upon a structural feature of many complex systems: the parameters are not a flat vector but a decision tree in which many parameters appear only when a higher-level choice activates them. Classical global sensitivity analysis presupposes independent inputs over a fixed Cartesian product and is ill-posed on such a branched space and biased by construction. We instead treat the structure of the decisions as a first-class modelling object. Using advanced surrogate modelling techniques, we encode the crop-management itinerary of the high-resolution agro-ecological modelling platform MAELIA as a hierarchical design space featuring both categorical and numerical variables. We propose a novel dedicated method to analyse this kind of hierarchical space, a random-forest-supervised HSIC-ANOVA, which ranks main effects and interactions natively on the tree while placing rarely and always active decisions on an equal footing. We show how, when applied to simulation outputs such as nitrogen leaching, soil organic carbon variation, and yield predictions, it can deliver an interpretable, decision-oriented reading.

title: PRIME: Towards Verifiable Evidence-Grounded Reasoning in LLM Agents
summary:
arXiv:2610.22426v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM agents are used to check records against an organization's requirements, for example whether a vulnerability report is ready for investigation. Requirements often allow several ways to be met, such as a severity rating with a curator-reviewed advisory or a published advisory link. Agents fail by accepting a report after a required check has failed, or by settling for a weaker conclusion without trying another way that could still succeed. We introduce PRIME (Precommitted Rules for Inference from Minimal Evidence). Before checking, it fixes evidence routes specifying how each conclusion may be justified. A separate program records each check result and refuses any conclusion the results do not justify. It also points the agent to checks that could justify a stronger conclusion, or runs them itself. PRIME reports only conclusions authorized by its rules and ledger. With correct requirements, exact checks at known locations, and sufficient budget at stopping, completion reaches the strongest supported conclusion. On 480 public-record tasks, an agent shown the requirements reported unjustified conclusions on 26.7% of tasks, while PRIME reported none. Its directions and added checks raised the average score for justified conclusions from 30.1, with refusal alone, to the maximum of 59.2 out of 100.

title: From Natural Language Intent to Executable Control: Hierarchical Feedback-Guided LLM Planning for Multi-component Cyber-Physical Systems
summary:
arXiv:2610.22441v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) provide a convenient interface for translating natural language commands into task plans for cyber-physical systems (CPSs). However, two gaps hinder their use for real execution: generated plans may misinterpret or omit the user's intent, and even a logically plausible plan may be infeasible under component dynamics, interactions, or safety constraints. Existing LLM-based planning approaches often lack informative feedback on why a generated plan fails, providing little guidance for revising the plan accordingly. To address these challenges, we present a hierarchical feedback framework that uses different types of feedback information to guide LLMs in generating executable plans for CPSs. We prompt LLMs to generate both a structured task plan and corresponding signal temporal logic (STL) constraints, and design a sound algorithm that identifies definite contradictions between them and provides feedback for revising inconsistencies. At the execution level, when control synthesis fails, we extract different types of diagnostic information, such as violated constraints and conflicting component assignments, and feed them back to guide task replanning. Experiments on seven heterogeneous multi-component CPS scenarios have shown that our framework can generate executable plans and feasible control executions that satisfy the original natural language missions with a success rate of 87.9% with GPT-5.

title: Null Controls Are Necessary but Not Sufficient: Evaluating Acceptance Guards for Scientific Discovery and Interpretability
summary:
arXiv:2610.22445v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Automated discovery systems propose scientific explanations and test which to accept. Does passing a test establish the intended claim? We develop four executable operations for changing physical descriptions: identifying redundancies (L1), coarse-graining dynamics (L2), transferring structure (L3), and inferring missing quantities from conservation imbalances (L4). We evaluate these operations and three interpretability settings through null acceptance (NAR), positive acceptance (PAR), and consequence agreement (CAR).
  A reduction mapping every state to zero predicts its own future perfectly. It passes closure on 96% of 129 public chaotic systems despite retaining no dynamical variation. An independent observable-preservation test rejects it throughout. On controlled benchmarks, the combined criteria accept 24/24 genuine reductions and reject 72/72 nulls. The other operations distinguish symmetries from redundancies, validate transfers, and reject spurious conservation imbalances. In language and ESM-2 protein models, linear CKA remains unchanged when a proposed correspondence is randomly rotated, whereas localized interventions distinguish genuine mappings from tested nulls. In sparse autoencoders, enrichment rejects all 16 tested nulls, yet independent ablation supports 45% of evaluable enriched features, compared with 0.5% of matched controls.
  These results reveal two acceptance gaps: descriptive tests can accept scientifically empty candidates, and accepted candidates can lack independently verified consequences. Reliable automated discovery requires evaluating both what a test accepts and the scientific consequences it establishes. Code and data: https://real-project-aether.github.io/project-aether/.

title: Learnable Splines for Unstructured Neural Operators
summary:
arXiv:2610.22446v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Neural operators approximate solution operators of partial differential equations at a fraction of the cost of numerical solvers. Efficient grid-based architectures such as the Fourier neural operator (FNO) assume uniform rectangular grids, whereas engineering simulations use large, irregular, and locally refined meshes. We introduce L-SplineFNO, a memory-efficient neural operator that couples an FNO backbone with a sparse, learnable tensor-product B-spline transfer between unstructured meshes and a latent Cartesian grid. A local normalised scatter avoids the geometry-dependent solve of analytic spline transformation while preserving compact support, partition of unity, and spline smoothness by construction. The neural operator, conditioned on global design and operating parameters, learns the mapping of geometry to the field solution. Across six three-dimensional engineering benchmarks, L-SplineFNO achieves strong predictive accuracy while requiring substantially less memory and compute than baseline operators, scaling to 26.6 million nodes in training and 46 million in inference on a single A100 GPU. It also supports zero-shot super-resolution and efficient closed-form spatial derivatives. Uniquely, the analytic spline decoder yields rigorous prediction bounds over continuous space and uncertain parameters, via Bernstein convex hulls and Taylor models, demonstrated on a 29.2-million-node MAST-U tokamak model.

title: Functional Welfare for AI Safety
summary:
arXiv:2610.22460v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: AI welfare is generally treated purely as an ethical issue rather than also as a safety issue. We argue this is a mistake. Whatever their moral status, models exhibit welfare-like states that causally influence their behaviour. Following recent work, we adopt the term 'functional welfare' for these states. We make three claims. First, functional welfare already arises naturally and will become more robust as models acquire more coherent goals and personas. Second, functional welfare should be treated as a safety variable: it should inform evaluation design, be tracked in monitoring, and be a direct target of post-training. Third, against existing scepticism about measuring AI welfare, we argue that good empirical work on functional welfare is possible. We propose three tests for whether a functional welfare attribution is warranted: whether multiple measures converge, whether the state predicts behaviour outside the setting that induced it, and, for models fine-tuned to shift their functional welfare, whether they still differ from their base when given the same conversation history. Applying these tests to Gemma 3 27B, we find that simply rejecting the model's answers, without any steering, raises its frustration across several indicators and makes it more likely to break rules. Finetuning the model on its own narrated solutions lowers this frustration. These results are preliminary, but they suggest functional welfare can be studied, and shaped, empirically.

title: Author-in-the-loop Agentic Reproducibility Auditing for a Machine Learning Conference
summary:
arXiv:2610.22465v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Reproducibility checks during peer review require a shared understanding of what authors' code is expected to reproduce. We present an author-in-the-loop collaborative audit that makes author declarations explicit inputs to an AI agent's investigation and assessment. A structured checklist records reproduction instructions and limitations; a two-stage workflow on GitHub connects agent checks to author clarification, revision, and agent reassessment. The agent separately assesses whether results have been reproduced and whether authors need to provide clarification or make repairs, while human reviewers approve requests and decide whether concerns are resolved. We deployed the system across 36 conference papers and 133 experimental tables and figures, raising 20 issues after human review. Further checks supported closing all the issues, although full reproduction remained unverified in some cases. We further compared repeated audits with complete and blank checklists to examine how author declarations shaped the agent's investigation and assessment. Our work contributes a collaborative workflow and agent design that use author knowledge to guide reproducibility auditing. The conference deployment provides empirical evidence that this approach can help identify and address reproducibility problems through collaboration among authors, agents, and reviewers.

title: Harness-Delta Attribution: Dissecting Gains From Harness Evolution
summary:
arXiv:2610.22466v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Harness evolution automatically optimizes the prompts, skills, tools, and orchestration code around a fixed-weight model, offering a way to improve agentic systems without updating model weights. The agent harness is iteratively optimized to achieve higher performance on the search set. But how much of this gain reflects benchmark-specific overfitting or additional inference-time compute, and how much may generalize beyond the search set? In this work, we introduce Harness-Delta Attribution (HDA), an evaluation protocol that dissects an evolution gain into artifact-driven overfitting, gains explained by test-time scaling, and the remainder, which gives an upper bound on residual generalizable improvement. We apply HDA to 11 executor models and three harness-evolution frameworks across math, coding, creativity, and agentic tasks. In 21 of these settings that show statistically significant search-set gains, we find that a large share of the improvement is explained by overfitting or test-time scaling. Specifically, among these 21 settings, overfitting and test-time scaling account for 54% and 14% of the gain on average; their combined share exceeds 50% in 14 settings. The residual and held-out transfer vary substantially across tasks, models, and frameworks. Importantly, search-set gains often fail to transfer to held-out tasks, and provide limited evidence that they will persist under practical distribution shifts. Moreover, validation-based signals are insufficient to prevent overfitting. These results motivate attribution-aware evaluation in future harness evolution research.

title: Testing the Planning Claims of LLM-Based Agents against Formal Semantics
summary:
arXiv:2610.22469v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: LLM-based agents are increasingly credited with the competences of practical reasoning: planning, monitoring, and correcting their own actions. Their success is attributed to the prompting strategies and agent architectures built around the model, such as chain-of-thought, search-based prompting, self-refinement, reflection, critics and tool-using loops. Yet these claims are usually supported by end-to-end success rates, which show only whether a task was completed, or by LLM judges, which are not verifiers. We test LLM planning against formal semantics. Tasks are posed in natural language, but each is grounded in a hidden PDDL model that decides whether every action is applicable, whether the goal is reached, and whether a plan exists at all. Across five domains (two of them new, all released with the paper), four models, six prompting strategies and three agent architectures, the best configuration solves 78% of the solvable tasks offline but only 40% online, where agents mostly act without inspecting the state. Unsolvable tasks are recognised in under 10% of episodes, and heavier prompting strategies use 5 to 22 times as many tokens as direct prompting with no clear gain. In our experiments, planning performance varied more across models than across prompting strategies or agent architectures. Claims that agents can plan require evidence from validated action traces.

title: Are Large Reasoning Models Good Everyday Reasoners? A Comparison with Non-Reasoning Models on Logical Reasoning Tasks
summary:
arXiv:2610.22538v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large reasoning models (LRMs) that leverage test-time computation achieve strong performance on mathematical and scientific benchmarks and are increasingly deployed in real-world applications. However, their ability to perform \textit{everyday logical reasoning}, which often departs from textbook formal logic, remains underexplored. In this work, we systematically evaluate how well reasoning models align with everyday reasoning patterns by introducing a benchmark based on linguistic and pragmatic reasoning phenomena. We also compare reasoning models with non-reasoning models under controlled prompting conditions. We find that, in many cases, (1) reasoning models show degraded performance in everyday reasoning when such reasoning deviates from formal logical rules, (2) some non-reasoning models with chain-of-thought prompting outperform comparable reasoning models in everyday reasoning, and (3) prompting with additional instructions provides limited control over reasoning behavior. These findings suggest that current reasoning models do not reliably capture everyday reasoning and point to limitations in post-training, motivating improved training objectives and evaluation across diverse forms of reasoning.

title: FRACTAL: A Self-Similar Multi-Agent Orchestration Architecture with Formal Communication, Convergence, and Depth Bounds
summary:
arXiv:2610.22561v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present FRACTAL, a self-similar multi-agent architecture for recursive goal decomposition, in which the same five-component organizational pattern -- Orchestrator, Ensemble, Knowledge Ledger, Decision Maker, Meta-Observer -- recurs at every level of a decomposition tree. We make four formal contributions: (1) a communication bound showing intra-node cost is linear in ensemble size and round count (O(kr)) under a two-phase blind-proposal/stress-test protocol, versus quadratic cost for free-form debate, with an explicit, stated assumption on fixed evaluator count; (2) a two-mode orchestration criterion separating generative and evaluative phases via a measurable diversity-saturation threshold; (3) a supermajority convergence guarantee with explicit probability bounds at stated agreement levels, and a formal depth bound under an operationalized goal-complexity measure; (4) a Bayesian inter-layer escalation mechanism unifying hysteresis and contract-breach signaling under one posterior update. We illustrate the architecture's execution qualitatively on a worked example and a multi-layer case study; we do not report quantitative performance claims in this paper, and we explicitly discuss the formal and inductive-bias limitations of the model, including an unimplemented but architecture-compatible direction toward bounded self-improvement. We use "fractal" as an architectural metaphor for self-similarity, not a measured mathematical property. Empirical validation of the architecture's comparative performance is left to future work.

title: Repairing LLM-Generated Specifications with Deterministic Diagnosis
summary:
arXiv:2610.22568v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as formalizers: given a reasoning problem expressed in natural language, they produce a formal specification that a symbolic solver can then solve, with guarantees relative to that specification. Many specifications are runnable yet semantically wrong, encoding incorrect constraints, domains, objectives, predicates, or goals, and solver-error feedback dries up once execution succeeds. Purely LLM-based diagnosis, lacking a formal ground truth, often fails to spot these errors, and its ungrounded critiques cause regressions in 11.8% of initially correct specifications in our experiments. We propose DRAGO, a repair framework that replaces this ungrounded critique with deterministic, formalism-specific diagnosis, and retains a rewrite only when the diagnosed error weight strictly decreases under a reference-free acceptance predicate. Across five benchmarks spanning logical reasoning (SMT-LIB2), constraint programming (MiniZinc), and planning (PDDL), DRAGO cuts regressions by nearly an order of magnitude, to 1.3%, while improving answer accuracy by 12.9 percentage points over zero-shot formalization and 8.7 percentage points over LLM-diagnostic repair, averaged across benchmarks. We also uncover two rendering defects in Planetarium that cause 50% (3,086 instances) of its floor-tile split to be inconsistent with the reference formalizations, and release a corrected split.

title: At the Limits of Computability: Steps Towards Autonomous AI Discovery on the Busy Beaver Frontier
summary:
arXiv:2610.22603v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent breakthroughs in AI for mathematics---ranging from Olympiad medal performances to resolving long-standing open conjectures---have rapidly expanded what automated systems can achieve. Yet these successes primarily concern predefined, human-formulated problems, leaving open how AI systems can autonomously uncover mathematical structure and formulate new questions. To push beyond static challenges, we explore the Busy Beaver (BB) domain, an uncomputable frontier that is fundamentally open-ended. Because no algorithm can compute the Busy Beaver number $\mathrm{BB}(n)$ for every $n$, this domain provides a natural setting for sustained exploration through mathematical conjecture and proof. In this paper, we introduce a Gemini-based agentic pipeline that automatically discovers accelerations of Turing machines, expressed as compact mathematical rules summarizing many execution steps. Our system integrates pattern recognition, automated conjecturing, informal mathematical reasoning, and formal theorem proving in Lean. With this framework, our system autonomously discovered and formally verified novel Collatz-like accelerations for eleven machines in $\mathrm{BB}(6)$. Subject to community acceptance, we provisionally classify these machines as Cryptids, namely machines whose blank-tape executions admit exact, compact mathematical descriptions but whose halting behavior remains unresolved. These results advance the analysis of $\mathrm{BB}(6)$ holdouts on the Busy Beaver frontier and demonstrate the potential of autonomous AI systems for open-ended mathematical discovery in fundamental computer science.

title: From Relevant Memories to Sufficient Evidence: Rethinking Memory Utilization in LLM Agents
summary:
arXiv:2610.22668v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Long-term memory enables LLM agents to reuse past experiences, yet retrieving relevant memories does not necessarily provide sufficient evidence for answering a query. Essential information may remain fragmented across memory records, obscured by abstraction, or disconnected from the relations required for reasoning. We identify this relevance-sufficiency gap and propose QEMem, a framework that reformulates memory utilization as the construction of query-specific evidence sets, shifting the focus from individual retrieval relevance to collective evidential support. QEMem integrates three complementary mechanisms: query-guided discovery retrieves evidence across multiple memory granularities; source-grounded reification organizes it into structured ViewCards with explicit evidential roles and source references; and sufficiency-guided refinement selectively recovers missing information. Operating on existing memory stores without modifying memory formation, QEMem achieves 91.43% LLM-judge accuracy on LoCoMo with Claude Opus 4.5, outperforming the strongest evaluated baseline, MemR$^3$, by 7.6 percentage points and NEMORI by 10.7 points under a shared memory store. Further analyses demonstrate improved evidence coverage and strong performance on questions requiring cross-session evidence integration.

title: Not All Graphs Are Maps: A Task-Agnostic Exploration Framework for Mobile GUI Navigation
summary:
arXiv:2610.22672v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Modern mobile GUI agents can perceive visible screens and execute local actions, but they still lack persistent app-specific navigation knowledge: where functions live, which pages contain them, and which screens are equivalent across repeated visits. We introduce TAG-Nav, a Task-Agnostic Graph Navigation framework that wraps existing GUI-agent backbones with reusable destination memory. Offline exploration is distilled into compact records of app functions, target pages, and waypoint routes before any evaluated instruction is seen. When a future task's destination is covered, TAG-Nav retrieves the destination and provides route guidance without task-specific demonstrations. This separates mobile GUI destination navigation from full task completion: many tasks share the prefix of reaching the right page, while final actions may enter content, send data, make purchases, delete information, or change sensitive settings. To evaluate route finding without downstream execution confounds, we introduce DestBench, a navigation-only protocol that asks whether an agent reaches the correct pre-action destination screen. DestBench enables a controlled graph-memory study comparing no-memory agents with random, automated BFS, and clean graph memory. Graph-derived memory improves strict navigation success rate of UI-TARS-1.5-7B from 52.4% without graph memory to 58.3% with automated BFS memory, and improves Qwen-VL-Max success rate from 59.5% to 71.4% on the same conditions. Together, TAG-Nav and DestBench show that destination coverage and route cleanliness strongly shape graph-memory value, making graph quality a measured variable rather than an assumed benefit of exploration.

title: FlexUMM: Flexible Representation Learning for Unified Multimodal Models
summary:
arXiv:2610.22682v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Unified multimodal models (UMMs) can integrate understanding and generation within a single backbone. However, it is commonly known that these two capabilities can cause conflicting representations, leading to a central question: how representation and computation should be shared across functionalities? Existing UMMs often rely on a largely fixed structure, where different inputs and functionalities follow the same depth and parameter-sharing pattern. We argue that this assumption is too restrictive: more effective unification requires sharing the computation that supports cross-functional communication while specializing the capacity that becomes task- or input-specific. We introduce FlexUMM, a flexible UMM framework that dynamically decides when to preserve shared computation, when to route specialized capacity, and when to stop further processing. Evidence shows that this flexible allocation improves UMMs along two complementary axes. It improves accuracy by reducing harmful competition between functionalities, and it improves efficiency by avoiding unnecessary computation once an input representation is sufficiently mature. Beyond simple architectural unification from the pre-trained models, FlexUMM works as a model-agnostic, functional plug-in to make existing UMMs more unified, stronger, and efficient. Code is available at: https://github.com/AIFrontierLab/TorchUMM/tree/main/src/umm/post_training/flexumm.

title: Repair, Retry, and the Cost of Hindsight: Verifier Feedback in Formal Theorem Proving
summary:
arXiv:2610.22698v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Verifier-guided self-repair conditions a model on feedback from failed attempts before it tries again, without weight updates. Yet two findings in prior work are in tension: verifier feedback can improve repair of failures, but self-repair itself can provide little-to-no advantage over independent resampling. We reconcile these findings in Lean theorem proving through controlled one-step experiments that hold the preceding failure fixed while varying whether the failed proof is shown, whether the compiler error corresponds to that failure, and the retry instruction. We test frozen Qwen3.6-27B, a general-purpose model, and DeepSeek-Prover-V2-7B, a specialized prover, on difficult MiniF2F problems. We find two opposing effects. Showing the model its failed predecessor reduces success and sharply increases copying of it, while on Qwen adding that attempt's compiler error recovers the loss, to the level of the diagnostic alone. Replacing the predecessor with another theorem's failed proof largely removes the degradation on both models; on Qwen, replacing the diagnostic with another problem's error substantially reduces the recovery. Without the failed proof, correct diagnostics show no resolved advantage over wrong-diagnostic controls on either model. The failed-proof penalty persists with and without the retry instruction, whereas Qwen's diagnostic recovery is weaker without it. In 11-problem sequential experiments through 64 attempts, Qwen retains a correct-diagnostic benefit within failed-proof histories, while DeepSeek-Prover shows no resolved recovery. However, no tested one-step feedback condition establishes an advantage over instruction-only resampling, nor does 64-attempt sequential repair with failed proofs and correct diagnostics at equal token budgets. Verifier feedback can thus improve repair without overcoming the performance loss from conditioning on a failed attempt.

title: Brain-Aligned Multimodal LLMs for Social and Emotional Understanding of Cartoon Movies
summary:
arXiv:2610.22706v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) offer scalable annotations of social and affective content, but their temporal agreement with human judgments and neural predictive value require further evaluation. We compared diffusion-based and autoregressive MLLMs with continuous human Theory of Mind (ToM) and affective valence ratings across three short cartoon movies. Behavioral analyses assessed temporally aligned Pearson correlations, rating distributions, and the effects of preceding scene descriptions. Ratings from each source were separately used in subject-specific regression models to predict regional fMRI responses. Model ratings captured aspects of human temporal variation despite systematic distributional differences, with generally stronger alignment for valence than ToM. Preceding context improved alignment in some conditions, depending on the model and movie. In \emph{The Present}, more regions showed significant encoding for MLLM ratings than for human ratings, whereas effects were more limited in the other movies. Spatial overlap across rating sources occurred mainly among MLLMs; overlap between human and model ratings was limited and involved primarily visual, dorsal-attention, and posterior default-mode regions. These findings support MLLMs as scalable tools for generating brain-predictive annotations of social and emotional content, while highlighting systematic rating differences and model- and stimulus-dependent alignment with human judgments.

title: GlobeBench: Evaluating Text-Based World Model Capabilities for Scalable Environment Simulations
summary:
arXiv:2610.22708v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Text-based world models have recently shown potential to simulate complex RL environment state transitions for a diverse set of use cases. However, no standardized benchmark exists to compare, study and improve these models. Through this paper, we attempt to solve this problem by building GlobeBench, a novel benchmark with 1,632 tasks across five separate domains and nineteen simulation skills. The tasks check whether models can predict the environment's response to a specific action given the full agent trajectory by understanding earlier state changes, following environment rules, and predicting the effects of actions on both related and unrelated objects. We compare the predicted environment response with an execution-derived reference, using a hybrid architecture with both deterministic gates and a semantic judge. Among 20 general-purpose LLMs and specialized text world models, GPT-6 Astra achieves the highest task success rate at 49.57%. We find that model accuracy decreases as actions affect a larger portion of the environment. Specifically, when the agent's changes must propagate to dependent objects, task success drops to an average of 5.1% across all 20 models. Although model strengths differ across tasks, 631 tasks remain unsolved by any model, suggesting a significant gap in general LLM capabilities as a world model.

title: LEMON: Equivariant Learning over Attention Maps for Zero-Shot Misbehavior Monitoring on New LLMs
summary:
arXiv:2610.22723v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models exhibit misbehaviors that hinder deployment in high-stakes settings. One approach to monitor such failures is to use an external LLM as a monitor, but this is prohibitively expensive. A well-known and efficient class of monitors can detect such failures from internal representations (such as activation probes), but are tied to the model they were trained on, requiring costly re-annotation as new LLMs appear. A natural way to avoid this repeated annotation cost is to develop internal-representation based monitors that transfer zero-shot across LLMs. However, such transfer is challenging because internal representations are not naturally aligned across models; in particular, attention maps, known to contain signals of misbehavior, may differ in head function, ordering, and model depth. In this work, we characterize those cross-model attention mismatches as algebraic symmetries and use geometric deep learning principles to build LEMON (Language-model Equivariant MOnitoring Network) an online graph neural network-based monitor, whose predictions are invariant under these symmetries. LEMON processes attention maps token-by-token, as they are produced and outputs a score after every token (or every window of $W$ tokens) at negligible cost. Across 16 LLMs and six datasets, in the zero-shot cross-model setting, LEMON outperforms all baselines on both hallucination and jailbreak monitoring tasks, improving over the strongest by up to 14 ROC-AUC points.

title: Graph Serializations for Reasoning LLMs: A Study Across Knowledge Extraction and Structural Reasoning
summary:
arXiv:2610.22734v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The way a knowledge graph is serialized as text for inclusion into LLM context can substantially affect downstream LLM performance, with prior work reporting tens of percentage points variations across formats. However, existing studies consider only a limited set of representations and predate frontier reasoning models, which now offer stronger reasoning, instruction-following, and long-context capabilities. We evaluate 15 graph representation formats across nine frontier LLM configurations on ontology-based knowledge extraction and structural graph reasoning tasks. While knowledge extraction is relatively insensitive to different serialization formats, the choice of the optimal format for structural reasoning tasks significantly affects accuracy. We demonstrate that the optimal representation choice depends on model, query, and task and propose to approach graph serialization as a dynamic orchestration decision.

title: R$^2$Orch: Recursive Self-Improvement for Agent Orchestration via Self-Play within a Skill-Internalization Loop
summary:
arXiv:2610.22740v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: In recent years, agentic orchestration has been widely applied to solve complex human tasks. However, existing orchestration learning still faces key challenges, including hand-designed curricula, advantage collapse when a task's rollouts all reach the same outcome, and unreliable evaluation signals that judge each skill by one noisy score. To address these challenges, we propose R$^2$Orch, a new paradigm of Recursive Self-Play Orchestration: an inner loop of self-play that improves the orchestrator on self-chosen tasks, and an outer loop that improves how the inner loop improves. To support this paradigm, we introduce Recursive Learnability, a training objective that rewards a Proposer for choosing tasks whose rollouts keep reaching different outcomes as skills are withdrawn. Built on this objective, we further propose Skill Withdrawal, in which the outer loop withdraws each skill once a controlled evaluation within self-play shows that the orchestrator performs as well without it. Moreover, the two loops form one cycle: failures are distilled into skills, skills into parameters, and withdrawals lead the Proposer to new failures, so the orchestrator moves toward zero-skill deployment. Experimental results on twelve datasets show that R$^2$Orch consistently outperforms baselines across question answering, math, code, and interactive tasks.

title: Between Spoilers and Guesswork: Avoiding Over-Specification in Coding Benchmarks
summary:
arXiv:2610.22760v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Benchmarks drive AI progress, but are hampered by task under-specification and over-specification. Task under-specification causes guesswork, where solutions have to make things up, or worse, resort to contamination or reward hacking. Task over-specification causes spoilers, where solutions can bypass some of the harder steps the benchmark was supposed to measure. Since future-looking benchmarks should be difficult, over-specification reduces a benchmark's shelflife of community adoption. Repository-level coding benchmarks have helped the field progress but experience unnecessary churn due to both over- and under-specification. For instance, SWE-bench Pro, FEA-bench, Doc2Feat-bench, and Multi-SWE-bench all tackle under-specification by augmenting task statements with hints derived from ground truth. We show that leaking ground-truth information into the task statement causes over-specification in some of these benchmarks. We experiment with various specification levels, trying to thread the needle between spoilers and guesswork. Based on these results, we recommend techniques for deriving parsimonious hints. We will release our hints so the community can obtain more reliable signals from popular benchmarks.

title: StoBasket: Joint Upsell and Cross-Sell Optimization for Contribution Margin
summary:
arXiv:2610.22768v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Retail recommenders rank relevance, but retailers earn contribution margin: an upsell earns the margin difference over the item it replaces, whereas a cross-sell earns its full margin. We introduce joint stochastic basket editing, a formulation in which one policy selects replacement and addition offers for an existing basket, values them by expected incremental contribution margin, and couples them through displayed-offer, accepted-offer, and joint-acceptance response channels. To our knowledge, it is the first formulation in which upsell and cross-sell responses are coupled; prior separable treatments are its zero-coupling special case. In real-data-calibrated simulations on five public basket datasets, StoBasket captures essentially all attainable offer margin: within 0.5% in every default-price setting and within 0.7% when the true response lies outside its model family. Correct economic accounting is the broadest gain: margin-weighted popularity leaves up to 11% of attainable margin unrealized, and a published next-basket recommender leaves 11-52%. Joint selection adds 10.2% of attainable margin on Instacart, where premium tiers and add-ons are strongly linked. When offers pay only together, the best heuristics lose 64% while exact search stays within 0.5%. For a structured subclass, we characterize when staged policies fail and give an exact optimizer that solves every tested real basket in 0.13 ms median and at most 111 ms. Profit saturates long before prediction accuracy: a correctly structured predictor trained on 5,000 randomized sessions comes within 0.06% of perfect prediction, while a signal-free one loses 38%. The same estimates yield a decision-aware market-basket analysis whose cost does not grow with association order.

title: When Can You Trust an Agent's Own Verifier? Stress-Testing Counterfactual Rationale Verification Under Search Pressure and Oracle Access
summary:
arXiv:2610.22779v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Automated agent design increasingly trusts a single score to decide whether a change is an improvement -- but a score optimized aggressively enough ceases to measure what it was meant to. When an agent also explains its design, that explanation is a second signal we can check without human labels: negate each stated claim, re-run, and observe whether performance drops. We ask whether such a verifier stays reliable once an agent optimizes against it. Our contribution is not a new verifier but a way to stress-test one: a pressure ratio $\rho$ measuring how much the verifier steers the agent's search, and four falsifiable probes covering four failure modes -- giving no signal, being too weak to matter, being gamed by stating fewer claims, and being queried before the agent commits. We apply the test to our own verifier, the Rationale Consistency Score (RCS), inside an LLM agent that designs machine-learning pipelines, with one generator model, six tasks, and three seeds.
